implications.says: the cart passed out by the town gate, and the berths lie inside the quay gate: it was not going to a vessel
it went up Mill Lane, where Mr. Garrick writes that the casks had been going to his cellar: it took them there
the first pass was signed at Saltmere while Mr. Pell was in London: he did not sign it
one hand signed all three, and it was not Mr. Pell's
J.P. on a pass of the Custom House that is not Josiah Pell's is Jonas Prout's
the casks left the bond store on passes the clerk signed
and they went to a cellar in the town, not aboard a ship: Mr. Prout let the brandy out of bond
the stove was cold, raked out and shut: the fire did not come from it
the books were heaped to burn and oil was brought up to them: the fire was laid
the iron chest was left locked with the duty money in it: the fire was not for that
the bond store was left unburnt, locked and sealed: the fire was not for the brandy
rules_out: the brandy in the bond store

implications.says: the fire was laid in the books before the ledger press and burned deepest there: it was meant for them
implications.concludes: the books of the ledger press

implications.says: the can is the Custom House's own, and its place in the lamp room cupboard was empty: the oil came from there
implications.concludes: the Custom House's own lamp room

implications.says: the door was unlocked between the watch's round and the morning, unforced, and there was no other way in: the fire-setter came by the street door with a key
implications.concludes: by the street door with a key

implications.says: the book has no round at one o'clock: the watch did not make every round
so what Crouch says, that he made every round, is not so
Sam Tully had him in sight on the mole from soon after one until the bell: he was there
and the pier-head is a quarter of an hour from the Custom House: he could not have been at both
the log has the bell at 1.45 by a clock that is right: it was first rung at a quarter to two
Mrs. Rowe's quarter past one was by the church clock, half an hour slow: by true time, a quarter to two
she was honest, and wrong by her clock
the landlord and the potboy both say he was not in the house when the bell rang: he was not
so what Mr. Prout told me, that he was still at the table, was not so
he left at a quarter past one by a clock that is right
gone at a quarter past one, not back when the bell rang at a quarter to two: half an hour
the doctor sat with him at Cliff House, a mile and a half from the quay, through those hours: he could not have been there
a man who cannot put his foot to the ground does not walk to the quay: he could not have been there
he sailed in the Marigold at 9.45 and was aboard her at midnight and at four
and nothing could cross the bar between 11.30 and 7.55: he could not have come ashore in the night
he went by the 7.40 and came back by the 8.05, and there is no other train: he was not at Saltmere in the night
by her own log she lay at Cardiff from the first to the sixth: she was not at Saltmere on the third
at noon it was an hour past low water, and the bar carries water only within two hours of high: she could not have sailed
the entry names a berth that did not exist until the first of October: it was not written on the third of September
the first entry has the brig at the New Quay when she lay at Cardiff: no export was made as it says
the second has her sail at noon over a bar she could not cross: no export was made as it says
the first entry was written a month or more after its date: that is no slip of the pen
rules_out: a clerk's honest slips of date

implications.says: on each of the three nights the casks went out by the town gate to Mr. Garrick's cellar: none of them went aboard a ship
rules_out: a clerk's honest slips of date

implications.says: an entry of an export that was not made: these are not true exports
three entries of brandy exported, and the brandy went to a cellar in the town: the entries are false
two exports that could not have been made, and one of them written up a month late: the entries are false
so what the ledger says of the Marigold is not so
he came home without it: it was not at Cliff House
he left it on its peg in the lobby and came home without it: it hung in the Custom House
the fire went for the books of the ledger press, and the bond ledger was not among them
Mr. Pell had taken it and told nobody: the fire-setter did not know it was gone
whoever sent the boy knew the pier-head lamp wanted oil, and only Mr. Prout had been told: he sent him
and the message took the watch off the quay at one o'clock, when no round was made
the baker knew the man by the cloak and saw no face, and the cloak hung where anyone inside could take it: the man need not have been the Collector
and Mr. Pell was at Cliff House with the doctor: it was not he
what the baker saw stands; that it was the Collector was his own conclusion, and wrong
Crouch was on the mole until the bell began: it was not he
whoever was inside had let himself in with a key, and the watch has neither of the two: it was not Crouch
the man had a key, and of the two who hold one it was not Mr. Pell; and Mr. Prout had been gone from the Anchor that half hour: it was he
only the press was heaped and fired: the fire had one aim, and it was not the Collector
rules_out: out of spite against the Collector

implications.says: the ledger held three false entries, and in two days the Surveyor was to compare every export entry with the vessels' papers: someone needed it gone before then
and the fire was set, and laid in the press where the ledger is kept: it was burned to destroy the bond ledger
Captain Venn was at sea: it was not he
Mr. Garrick was away by train: it was not he
Crouch was on the mole: it was not he
Mr. Pell had the ledger himself and was at Cliff House with the doctor: it was not he

the fire-setter came in with a key, there are two keys to the street door, Mr. Pell's and Mr. Prout's, and by his own word Mr. Prout's never left his pocket: whoever let himself in was one of those two
it was burned to destroy the bond ledger, and the false entries in it were Mr. Prout's to hide: the fire was his to want
he had the reason, he cleared the quay of its watch, and he was seen coming out in the Collector's cloak: Mr. Prout set the fire
of the two who could have let themselves in, it was not Mr. Pell: Mr. Prout set the fire
